children: Gold ETF inflows bounced back sharply in August, at a time when gold prices also staged a strong rally during the month.

Gold exchange-traded funds attracted Rs 2,596.70 crore in net inflows in August, up nearly 67 percent from Rs 1,558.75 crore in July, according to the latest data from the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI).

The fresh numbers come as gold continues to trade at elevated levels. On September 10, MCX gold futures for the October contract were trading around Rs 1,53,679 per 10 grams in morning trade, while domestic spot gold had closed the previous session at Rs 1,52,764 per 10 grams.
Gold ETF flows rebound after July fall
The August increase follows a sharp slowdown in Gold ETF flows during July.

Gold ETFs had attracted Rs 3,443.23 crore in June, before inflows more than halved to Rs 1,558.75 crore in July. At Rs 2,596.70 crore, August inflows have recovered substantially, although they are still about 25 percent below June levels.
The three-month trend shows that money has continued to come into Gold ETFs, but the pace of inflows has moved sharply from one month to another.
Gold gained 9% in rupee terms in August
The rise in Gold ETF inflows also coincided with a strong month for the yellow metal.

Gold gained 9 percent in Indian rupee terms during August, ending the month at around Rs 1,55,114 per 10 grams, according to the World Gold Council. In US dollar terms, gold gained 13.3 percent during the month to end at $4,563 an ounce. August was the metal's third-strongest monthly return in a quarter century in dollar terms.
That distinction matters for Indian investors: while the global gold rally was stronger in dollar terms, the relevant return for domestic investors was around 9 percent in rupee terms.
The AMFI data does not establish that the price rally caused the increase in Gold ETF investments, but the two trends moved together during August.
Gold makes up a fourth of ETF inflows
AMFI's revised classification also gives a clearer picture of how money moved across different types of ETFs in August.
ETFs received a total of Rs 10,160.87 crore during the month. Equity ETFs attracted the largest amount at Rs 7,237.49 crore, while Gold ETFs received Rs 2,596.70 crore.
Silver ETFs attracted another Rs 1,270.63 crore, while debt ETFs recorded net outflows of Rs 944.97 crore. Hybrid ETFs received a marginal Rs 1.02 crore.
Gold ETFs therefore accounted for roughly 26 percent of total ETF net inflows during August.
Global Gold ETF buying also surged
The pickup was not limited to India.
Globally, gold-backed ETFs attracted $18 billion in August, the second-largest monthly inflow in value terms on record, according to the World Gold Council.

North American and European-listed funds drove the increase. Europe received $7.9 billion, its strongest month on record, while North American funds attracted around $7.7 billion, their third-largest monthly inflow.
Strong inflows and higher gold prices pushed global Gold ETF assets under management 16 percent higher to $615 billion. Collective holdings increased by 121 tonnes to a record 4,189 tonnes.
What should investors make of the numbers?
For Indian investors, August therefore brought together two notable developments: Gold ETF inflows rebounded 67 percent and domestic gold prices gained 9 percent during the month.

But monthly fund flows and recent returns alone should not determine whether an investor increases exposure to gold. Gold ETFs are one way of taking exposure to domestic gold prices without holding physical gold, and their role in a portfolio is typically linked to diversification rather than simply chasing a recent price rally.
For now, the AMFI numbers show a clear reversal from July's slowdown: Gold ETF inflows moved back above Rs 2,500 crore in August, even though they remained below the Rs 3,443 crore received in June.
